objective: Take up sub-goal B125, given the go-ahead by the coordinator on 2026-11-10 (G1 with G5): prove that a plane of rule-60 rings grown by the doubling law reads, in conformal time (a lag after k doublings counted as 2^-k, A56), its original rings' taxicab distance up to a bounded additive error, for every schedule and every size, so that its conformal round trip time lengths are a metric up to a constant; and say whether the 4g 2^k crossing law is a consequence of the construction.
status: Complete 2026-11-10 (sub-goal B125): proved that for every doubling schedule from the open n x n tube and every size, in conformal time (a lag after k doublings counted as 2^-k, A56), the first arrival between original rings is 4g times their taxicab distance up to -6g and +9g + 2, so the conformal round trip is a metric up to 42g + 4; the one-stage earliest arrivals are a taxicab distance on the contact lattice (two quarter-turn hops per ring step), which gives the 4g 2^k law in a line. Checked against breadth-first search (326,400 pairs) and 15,373 route arrivals; plain lags have unbounded excess (computed). Recommendation Research directions (sharp constants).
stop_rule: Stop at a proof of the one-stage lemma and the conformal theorem with the frozen constants, each checked by computation, or at the case and step where a bound fails, with the statement narrowed.
